sentence: This project uses plants as a model to find out how and why the length of telomeres varies between individuals in a population.
This project looks for how genetic variants and exposures such as air pollution, lead and infections interact to affect brain cells and Alzheimer's disease.
This project compares gene activity in patient kidney samples with gene activity in podocytes to learn how gene variants raise kidney disease risk.
This project studies how calcium taken up by mitochondria leads to damage in cochlear cells and to hearing loss.
This project studies the molecular steps that let neural stem cells rest and then start dividing again to make neurons or glia.
This project tries to find out when changes across the senses begin during early development and how neural circuits rearrange after sensory deprivation.
This project studies how salt-inducible kinase 3 controls fertility and the development of ovarian follicles in ovarian granulosa cells.
This project profiles gene expression in single brain cells in a rodent model of HIV to study how HIV and opioid use disorder interact.
This project builds a low-cost model that gives primary care providers genetics-related clinical decision support without expensive tools.
This project follows patients treated with immunotherapy for cancer over time to find out the benefits and harms of cannabis use.
This project uses zebrafish to find out how the choroid fissure of the eye forms and how signaling pathways and metabolism control that process.
This project studies whether per- and poly-fluoroalkyl substances are linked to breast cancer risk among women in a multiethnic group.
This project provides data management and statistical modelling to analyze immune responses after liver transplants in murine models and in humans.
This project tries to find ways to induce transplantation tolerance in nonhuman primates so that kidney transplant recipients do not need chronic immunosuppression.
This project combines a human mammary epithelium model, drug modelling and machine learning to predict how much opioid use disorder medication reaches infants during lactation.
This project studies how the protein alpha-synuclein changes ion channels and lipid signaling in nanodomains to cause nerve cell damage and cell death.
This project supports shared research facilities with instruments that use biophysical and structural biology methods to study normal and disease processes.
This project studies the differences among patients with inflammatory arthritis caused by immune checkpoint inhibitors and evaluates immunosuppressive treatments for it.
This project uses the chick lens to find the regulatory elements and transcription factors that control expression of a gene during eye development.
